card.statement:
[62]

The (dual) $\imath$ canonical basis on $\mathbb{V}^{\otimes d}$ (viewed as a ${\textbf{U}}^{\imath}$ -module) coincides with the (dual) quasi-parabolic KL basis on $\mathbb{V}^{\otimes d}=\bigoplus_{f}\mathbb{M}_{f}$ (viewed as an $\mathscr{H}_{B_{d}}$ -module).

The quasi-parabolic KL polynomials are by definition the transition matrix entries from the quasi-parabolic KL to the standard basis. An inversion formula for parabolic KL polynomials (theorems of Kazhdan-Lusztig and Douglass) can be generalized to the quasi-parabolic cases.
card.label: Theorem 4.2

paper.title: Quantum symmetric pairs
paper.abstract: This is a survey of some recent progress on quantum symmetric pairs and applications. The topics include quasi K-matrices, $\imath$Schur duality, canonical bases, super Kazhdan-Lusztig theory, $\imath$Hall algebras, current presentations for affine $\imath$quantum groups, and braid group actions.
